newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy says 1,500 Albania refugees have disappeared.
newsitem.headline: Italy says 1,500 Albania refugees have disappeared.

text.p: About 1,500 of the Albanians who fled to Italy since violence erupted in their country have slipped away from refugee centres, the Interior Ministry said on Friday.

"A total of 13,450 Albanians have reached the (Italian) coast since the beginning of the emergency," the ministry said in a statement. "Around 1,500 have left (reception centres) without giving any notice," the statement said.
It did not elaborate but the implication was that the 1,500 had become illegal immigrants, moving on to other parts of Italy or elsewhere in Europe.

Interior Minister Giorgio Napolitano said the fact so many had gone missing justified the government's policy of allowing only genuine refugees into the country and forcibly repatriating economic immigrants and "criminals".
"The emergence of this element confirms the necessity to have a severe selection...to work out people really in need of protection and to repel the others," Napolitano said.

Thousands of Albanians began fleeing to southeast Italy early in March in overcrowded, rickety boats from across the Adriatic. The government has said that genuine refugees will be allowed to stay in Italy no longer than three months.
Those Albanians who had left refugee centres without good reason could be repatriated before the end of that limit, the Interior Ministry said on Friday.
It added that 1,302 people had already been sent home.
Armed unrest erupted in Albania in late February when protests over the collapse of fraudulent investment schemes mushroomed into insurrection in much of the south.
